jobs.title: Permit Reviewer - Flexible Hours
jobs.description_text: Scope of the Role: We are recruiting US-based architects and certified plans examiners to evaluate the output of an AI system that performs automated building-code compliance review on architectural permit applications. The system ingests permit submissions — new builds, alterations, modifications — and issues a compliant or non-compliant determination for each applicable check, drawn from the International Building Code. Every determination comes with a cited code provision and a marked location on the drawing set showing the evidence relied upon. Your job is to tell us where the system got it wrong. You are applying the same judgment you already apply in plan review or permit preparation, to a set of determinations that have already been made. Where the system is correct, you confirm it. Where it is wrong, you correct it and the correction becomes training signal. This is expert review work, not data entry. There is no volume of repetitive clicking to grind through and no generalist labeling pool to compete with — the entire premise of the program is that these judgments cannot be made by anyone without real code expertise. What You’ll Own: Review and correct pass/fail verdicts, written rationales, and citation boxes on PDF plans using the in-tool editing toolkit. jobs.description_text: Scope of the Role: Progress in physical AI is gated as much by data design as by model architecture. Your leverage is scientific judgment about data: deciding what is worth capturing in the real world versus generating in simulation, how to weight a training mix across embodiments and sensors, and how to measure whether a policy will hold up outside the lab. Your conclusions will shape what our partners collect next. jobs.title: Research Scientist, Speech & Audio
jobs.description_text: Scope of the Role: Where models actually differ now is robustness across accents, noise, and code-switching; speaker diarization; the naturalness of generated speech; and latency under streaming. Measuring those honestly, and building the data that trains for them, is gated as much by data and evaluation design as by architecture. Innodata builds that data and those evaluations for the customers and frontier labs advancing speech and audio models, and we are hiring a Research Scientist to own the science behind it. You will partner directly with the customers and frontier labs building ASR, text-to-speech, speech-to-speech and conversational voice, diarization, and audio-language models, as interested in the data behind them as in the models themselves. Your work is judgment: which conditions and languages a benchmark must cover to be honest, what a transcription convention should be for a given objective, and when an automated metric can be trusted versus when a human ear is required. You will also partner closely with our transcription and linguistics lead, whose standards directly shape what the models learn. What You’ll Own: You will define how Innodata designs, structures, and evaluates audio data for speech and audio models, and you will validate those choices experimentally. jobs.title: Research Scientist, Video & Multimodal
jobs.description_text: Scope of the Role: Video is where multimodal models are weakest and hardest to grade. Temporal reasoning, long-form understanding, grounding events in time, and holding audio, video, and text together do not fall out of image benchmarks — and the evaluations for them are still immature. Closing that gap is gated as much by how we design data and evaluation as by architecture. Innodata builds that data and those evaluations for the customers and frontier labs advancing video and multimodal models, and we are hiring a Research Scientist to own the science behind it. You will partner directly with the customers and frontier labs building video understanding, video-language, and video-generation models, as interested in the data behind them as in the models themselves. Video spans two model families judged in completely different ways: models that understand video — answering questions, localizing events, grounding language in time — where the question is whether the answer is correct; and models that generate it, where fidelity, temporal coherence, and physical plausibility matter and no automatic metric is settled. You own the evaluation science for both, and knowing when model-based scoring can stand in for a human versus when it can't. Your conclusions shape what our partners measure and collect next. What You’ll Own: You will define how Innodata designs, structures, and evaluates video data for video and multimodal models, and you will validate those choices experimentally.

This role is responsible for maintaining transaction data rooms, tracking lender and lender’s counsel requirements, and ensuring project information moves efficiently from collection through funding. Working cross-functionally with Development, Real Estate, Legal, Engineering, Construction, and Asset Management — as well as external parties such as surveyors, developers, contractors, and consultants — the Finance Analyst keeps financing workstreams organized, on schedule, and audit-ready. This is a highly cross-functional, process-oriented role suited to someone who is organized, detail-driven, and comfortable managing multiple moving pieces at once. What You’ll Own Due Diligence Management – Prepare, populate, and maintain debt financing due diligence checklists for lender’s counsel review; track lender and lender’s counsel comments, questions, and diligence requests through resolution, coordinating required responses and curative actions. Data Room & Documentation – Organize, upload, and maintain documents within transaction data rooms, ensuring proper indexing, version control, and completeness and integrity of project information across diligence trackers, data rooms, and financing submissions. You'll sit at the center of MEI's employee experience in our NYC office and help build the connective tissue that keeps people connected to one another and to MEI — all while getting direct exposure to executive support, workplace operations, culture and events, and cross-office collaboration. In this role, you'll be responsible not just for making the day-to-day run exceptionally well, but for anticipating needs, connecting dots, and finding smarter ways to work as MEI grows. It's a strong fit for someone who's equally comfortable executing the details and thinking beyond them — proactive, resourceful, and eager to build a foundation that opens doors to broader responsibilities at MEI over time. jobs.title: Director, Battery Asset Management
jobs.location_raw: Charlottesville, VA; Moorestown, NJ; New York, NY; Richmond, VA; Tysons, VA
jobs.description_text: About Us Madison Energy Infrastructure is hiring a Director of Battery Asset Management to build and run the operating platform behind our national, distributed, battery fleet. We have 80 MW of batteries operating today across 30 sites and 5 states, expect that fleet to triple next year and double the following year, with $2 billion of battery deployment ahead of us. The goal is simple: get the operating system right now, while the fleet is still manageable, so that it works when at scale. About You You've spent years elbow-deep in battery systems — you can read a three-line diagram without help, and you know an OEM's manual well enough to push back on their own engineers. You've managed contracts and you've managed people, and you're just as comfortable owning a preventative maintenance program as you are picking up the phone when a site goes down. You'd rather build something from scratch than inherit someone else's system, and you want to own the numbers that come with that. Key Responsibilities In year one, expect to be a player-coach: you'll manage the Battery Asset Manager, but you'll also be hands-on yourself — on the phone with OEMs, troubleshooting failures remotely, reviewing alarms, negotiating O&M agreements, visiting sites, escalating warranty claims, and making sure batteries dispatch when they're supposed to. Working across the organization, the Technology Operations & Cybersecurity Lead partners closely with employees, business leaders, and the Digital team to deliver exceptional technology experiences while driving operational excellence. This individual also serves as the primary relationship manager for MEI's managed technology partners, including our IT Managed Service Provider (MSP), virtual Chief Information Security Officer (vCISO), and Managed Detection and Response (MDR/SOC) providers, ensuring services are coordinated effectively, priorities remain aligned with business needs, and initiatives are executed successfully. This is a highly visible, hands-on role that combines technology operations, cybersecurity, vendor management, and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, embraces ownership, and is energized by solving complex problems. jobs.description_text: The Role Following Madison’s groundbreaking Community Infrastructure announcement to develop 1 GW and mobilize up to $2 billion in capital, we are hiring a leader to own MEI’s relationships with utilities, ISOs/RTOs, and state utility regulators. This person will be critical in helping MEI shape the market rules and utility programs that determine whether distributed storage and solar can be interconnected, accredited, and compensated at the massive scale our plan requires. This person will own MEI’s influence in those proceedings — identifying which rules actually matter to our thesis, deciding where our effort is best spent, and working directly with utilities and commission staff to craft programs that work for the utility, the Digital Infrastructure Partners, the community, and MEI at the same time. A separate hire will own policy and government relations — legislative advocacy, executive branch engagement, and trade association strategy. The two roles will coordinate closely, but the mandate here is technical, program-level, and commercial. A model that returns a quantity a biologist, human or AI, can argue with; models that transfer to new contexts, compose into a downstream calculation, and can be checked against an independent measurement are often worth more than a more accurate one that returns an embedding. jobs.description_text: Your Impact at LILA Lila is redefining the future of biomedicine by combining large-scale automated data generation with scientific superintelligence. We are building the loop where AI, automation, and experimental biology co-evolve. We are seeking a Senior ML Scientist to connect that work to human medicine, building the systems that assess whether a clinical program's biology holds up. Three questions define the work. Is the mechanism well supported? What has actually been established about how this intervention is meant to work, and what has only been assumed. Does the mechanism operate in patients? Human genetics, expression, cohort and prior-trial evidence all bear on whether the biology that works in a model system is present, and rate-limiting, in the population being treated. Is the trial built for that mechanism? Endpoints that read out the right thing on the right timescale, biomarkers that measure what the mechanism actually does, and enrollment criteria that select patients in whom it is operative — or, very often, none of these. You will not answer these program by program yourself. You will build the systems that do it, drawing on the mechanistic models and structured biological evidence the rest of the group generates, and grounding them in human data.
